transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because things have been happening at work that are starting to get me in trouble. I’m a cashier, and at the register I’ll get stuck doing something that doesn’t really fit what’s going on—like tapping the scanner in a certain pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting.

Last week I got written up for it, so… I figured I should talk to someone.
When you get stuck tapping the scanner or holding your hand over the drawer, does it feel like you have to do it to relieve a thought or fear that something bad will happen if you don’t?

Not really like a specific fear, no. It’s more that I just get stuck doing it, like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or my hand just stays over the cash drawer even though the customer is waiting. It doesn’t fit what’s happening, and I know it looks bad. That’s what got me written up.
Right before the tapping or freezing happens, do you feel a buildup of tension or an urge that gets relieved when you do it?

No, I don’t really notice a buildup or an urge like that. It’s more like I just get stuck in it. I’ll be at the register and suddenly I’m tapping the scanner in a pattern, or my hand is just hovering over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting. It doesn’t feel like it fixes anything, it just… happens, and then I realize it’s not fitting the situation.
When this happens, do you feel detached from yourself or like things around you aren’t fully real?
I don’t think so. I don’t feel like I’m outside myself or like the store isn’t real. It’s more just that I get caught in the action, and then I notice it’s gone on too long.
When your hand stays over the cash drawer, does it feel like you physically can’t make it move?

Not exactly like my hand is paralyzed or anything. It’s more like I just freeze there, with my hand over the drawer, and it doesn’t match what I’m supposed to be doing. The customer’s waiting, and I know I need to move, but I get stuck for a bit. That’s part of what got me written up.
Do you ever hear voices when no one is there?

Yeah… I do. Most days I hear what sounds like a couple people talking off to the side of me. Sometimes it’s like someone calls my name from the stockroom, or says I rang something up wrong. But when I look, there’s nobody there, and other people don’t seem to hear it.
Do you believe someone is deliberately trying to interfere with you or send you messages at work?
I don’t really know about that. I haven’t noticed anything that makes me think someone at work is doing it on purpose or sending me messages. It just happens, and I’m not sure what to make of it.
